toxicity.Notes: healthy mice, four females and five males per group, five injections every other day; LD50 18.1 mg/kg (95% CI 13.9-25.8), a mouse was counted as dead when body weight loss exceeded 20%; survival 100% at 6 mg/kg and seven of nine at 12 mg/kg, other doses only in Figure 7 (not read); body weight stable at 6 mg/kg (the article's Figure S13, which the SI file received 2026-11-16 does not contain; that file holds no body weight figure, and its Figure S13 is the organ H&E the article calls Figure S10); cisplatin LD50 below 3 mg/kg in the same assay

organs.Notes: H&E of five organs from healthy mice given Ru-1 12 mg/kg against a DMSO control. The article calls this figure S10 and the SI file lists it as Figure S13; it is the same figure. The authors write that Ru-1 at doses up to 12 mg/kg caused no obvious damage to these organs, while cisplatin vacuolised the renal tubules. The 6 mg/kg arm of the same comparison is in Figure 8 of the article. Activation was dark before 2026-11-18, set to none per source. Schedule as recorded before 2026-11-19: 5 injections every other day.

logp.method_description: Log Po/w values of Ru-1 and Ru-2 were determined using the shake-flask method. The complexes were dissolved in water that was presaturated with n-octanol (for 24 h and left to stand until phase separation occurred). The UV–Vis spectrum for each sample was obtained, and the absorbances at the λmax of each compound were determined. Equal volumes of n-octanol were added to each sample solution, and the heterogeneous mixtures were shaken for 2 h before centrifuging at 4000 rpm for 1 min to achieve phase separation. The final absorbance of the aqueous phase at the λmax of each compound was determined, and their water–octanol partition coefficient was calculated. All experiments were performed in triplicate.
